question.problem:
From top to bottom, what are the missing expressions in the following polynomial division problem?

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\boxed{} \\  & x-7\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,7{x}^{2}+\phantom{0}0x-\phantom{00}6} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{7{x}^{2}-49x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\boxed{} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{49x-343}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,337\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
From top to bottom, what are the missing expressions in the following polynomial division problem?

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\boxed{\text{[math]\phantom{x^2 - x + 1}[/math]}} \\  & x+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+64\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,{x}^{2}+0x+64 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,{x}^{2}-x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\boxed{\text{[math]\phantom{x + 64}[/math]}} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x+1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,63\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x^2$-term and the $x$-term. So, we write it using zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
x^3+{\color{red}0}x^2 + {\color{red}0}x + 64
$$

Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-x+1 \\  & x+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+64\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,{x}^{2}+0x+64 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,{x}^{2}-x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,x+64 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x+1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,63\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing expressions are

$\qquad$ $x^2 - x + 1\quad$ and $\quad x + 64.$
